pages.title: Flight Club Guidelines 🦉
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Flight Club

Welcome to Flight Club 🦉🚀

Buckle up, future flyer! Flight Club is where you earn points by completing weekly movement challenges. The more you challenge yourself, the higher you'll climb the ranks. Are you ready to take flight?

1
How It Works
The Basics

Each week brings new Flight Club challenges — stretching, strength, balance, and movement activities for you to complete. Every time you finish a challenge, you earn Flight Points.

Your goal? Rack up points over the year and rise to the highest rank!

  • 🎯 Maximum score: 100 points
  • 🏆 5 ranks to climb (lowest to highest)
  • 🌟 Bonus points for completing every challenge in a month
2
The Ranks
From Nestling to Soaring Owl 🦉
🌌
Soaring Owl
(85–100 pts)
The top tier! You've mastered movement and you fly above the rest. Legendary!
🦉
Wise Owl
(70–84 pts)
Strong, focused, and skilled. You're a top flyer.
🪽
Gliding Owl
(50–69 pts)
Smooth flying! Keep going — Soaring Owl is in sight.
🐤
Fluttering Owl
(30–49 pts)
You've taken off! Keep practicing to build your wings.
🥚
Nestling Learner
(0–29 pts)
Just starting — that's perfect! Every challenge helps you grow.
3
Earning Points
How to Rack Them Up

💪 Daily Stretch Challenge

5 points per stretch you complete.

🌟 Perfect Monthly Participation

10 bonus points if you finish ALL of the challenges in a month!

🎓 End-of-Year Bonus

At the end of the course, your rank earns extra credit toward your final grade!

💡Did You Know?

Owls have AMAZING flexibility — they can turn their heads almost all the way around! Their flight is silent because of special feathers. Every Flight Club rank is named after these awesome athletes of the sky. 🦉

🌎Real-World Connection

This isn't about being the strongest or fastest kid in class. It's about YOUR progress. Every challenge you complete is a victory — and every Owl rank is something to be proud of. 🌟

4
Get Started
Your Mission

Look for "Flight Club" challenges in your weekly modules. They'll always have the bright pink Flight Club Challenge badge so you can spot them easily!

Each challenge tells you exactly what to do. Just complete it, submit your proof (video or guardian note), and watch your points add up. 📈

📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: What rank would you be PROUD to reach this year? What's your first step? 📝

→What's Next

Time to fly! Look for your first Flight Club challenge in this week's module. Let's GO! 🚀

Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Week 2

Activity: Movement Stations 🏃

Time to put your movement skills to the test! You're going to set up four mini "stations" — each one practices a different superpower. Ready, set, GO!

1
Setup
Get Your Space Ready

Find an open space — your bedroom, living room, backyard, or basement work great. Use tape, pillows, or just imaginary spots to mark each station!

2
Stations
Visit Each Station
1
🦩 Balance Station

Stand on ONE foot for 10 seconds. Try the other foot too. Can you do it with your eyes closed? 👀

2
🤹 Coordination Station

Toss a ball (or rolled-up socks!) up in the air and catch it. Try 5 times in a row without dropping it.

3
💪 Strength Station

Do 5 jumping jacks or 5 push-ups. Feel that burn? That's your muscles getting stronger!

4
🔋 Endurance Station

Run in place for 30 seconds without stopping. Notice how your breathing changes.

🏃Activity Cue

Optional Challenge: Go through all 4 stations TWICE. That's a full workout! 🔥

✅Check for Understanding

Cool Down & Reflect — answer these:

  • Which station felt the EASIEST for you?
  • Which station was the HARDEST?
  • How do your muscles feel right now?
→What's Next

Submit a video, photo, or written reflection showing what you did at each station!

Week 2

Week 2 Flight Club: Stretch & Relax 🦉

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Think you've got what it takes to flap your way up the ranks? Three stretches stand between you and your first Flight Points. Let's GO! 🚀

1
Reach for the Sky Stretch

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
  • Stretch both arms up as high as possible, reaching for the sky.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then relax.
  • Optional: Wiggle your fingers like you're grabbing stars! ⭐

Benefits: Stretches arms, shoulders, and back.

2
Hug Yourself Stretch

How to do it:

  • Wrap your arms around yourself like you're giving a big hug.
  • Gently pull your shoulders forward while keeping your back straight.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then switch arm positions (whichever arm was on top, switch it).

Benefits: Stretches shoulders and upper back.

3
Shoulder Rolls

How to do it:

  • Stand or sit up straight.
  • Slowly roll your shoulders FORWARD in a circular motion 5 times.
  • Then roll your shoulders BACKWARD 5 times.

Benefits: Loosens up the shoulders and neck.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating the challenges. The more you do, the more points you earn in Flight Club! 🌟

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which stretch felt the BEST in your body?
  • Did anything feel surprisingly tricky?

3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.2 · Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
Week 4

Create Your Own Warm-Up & Cool-Down Routine 🔥❄️

You've learned why warm-ups and cool-downs matter — now it's time to BUILD your own! This is your chance to design a routine that's perfect for YOU.

1
Goal
What You're Doing

Create your very own warm-up AND cool-down routine to show you understand why both are important.

2
Part 1
Show What You Know
1
What is a warm-up?

Write 1–2 sentences explaining what happens to your body during a warm-up.

2
What is a cool-down?

Write 1–2 sentences explaining how a cool-down helps your body after activity.

3
Part 2
Build Your Warm-Up

List 3 warm-up moves you would do before playing a game or running.

For each one, write what part of the body it helps!

Example: Jog in place — wakes up legs and heart. Arm circles — loosens shoulders. Toe touches — stretches back.

4
Part 3
Build Your Cool-Down

List 3 cool-down moves to help your body relax after being active.

For each one, write how it helps your body calm down.

Example: Butterfly stretch — relaxes legs. Deep breathing — slows heart rate. Shoulder rolls — releases tension.

🌎Real-World Connection

Pro athletes spend 10–15 minutes warming up AND cooling down for EVERY practice. Their routines are designed by coaches. Yours is designed by YOU. 💪

🏃Activity Cue

Submission: Type your answers, write them neatly on paper and upload a photo, or record a video showing each move!

→What's Next

Next up: Your Flight Club challenge!

Week 4

Week 4 Flight Club: Stretch It Out 🦋

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Ready for round two? Three new stretches, three more chances to earn Flight Points. Show those owls what you've got! 🦉

1
Toe Touch Stretch (Waterfall Stretch)

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with feet together.
  • Slowly bend forward and reach for your toes, keeping legs straight.
  • Let your arms "flow down" like a waterfall. 💧
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then slowly stand up.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings (back of the thighs) and lower back.

2
Butterfly Stretch

How to do it:

  • Sit on the floor with feet together and knees bent outward.
  • Hold your feet with your hands and gently push your knees toward the floor.
  • Keep your back straight and hold the stretch.
  • Optional: Pretend your legs are butterfly wings and gently flap them! 🦋

Benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

3
Flamingo Stretch (Quadriceps Stretch)

How to do it:

  • Stand tall and bend one knee, bringing your foot behind you.
  • Hold your ankle with your hand and keep your balance.
  • Keep your knees close together and hold for 10 seconds.
  • Switch legs and repeat.
  • Optional: Extend one arm forward like a flamingo's neck! 🦩

Benefits: Stretches the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and improves balance.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video showing all three! Earn those Flight Points. 🌟

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which stretch felt the best on your legs?
  • Could you balance during the flamingo stretch?

Week 6

Week 6 Flight Club: Strength Squad 💪

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Drop and give me... a Flight Club workout! Three strength moves coming up. Show those muscles who's boss! 🔥

1
Side Lunge Stretch (Skater Stretch)

How to do it:

  • Stand with feet wide apart.
  • Bend one knee and shift your weight to that side, keeping the other leg straight.
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then switch sides.
  • Optional: Pretend you're an ice skater gliding side to side! ⛸️

Benefits: Stretches inner thighs and hips.

2
Forearm Plank

How to do it:

  • Get into a plank position with forearms on the ground and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.
  • Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Push-Ups

How to do it:

  • Start by lying on your stomach with your hands flat on the floor next to your shoulders.
  • Push your body up so your arms are straight and only your hands and toes are touching the ground.
  • Keep your body in a straight line — don't let your back sag or your hips rise.
  • Bend your elbows and lower your body until your chest is close to the floor, then push back up.
  • Try 5 push-ups to start.

Benefits: Builds upper body strength.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video showing your strength moves! 💪

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which strength move challenged you the most?
  • Could you feel which muscles were working?

Week 8

Week 8 Flight Club: Cardio Blast ⚡

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Get your heart pumping and your blood flowing — three cardio challenges that turn your living room into a workout zone! 🎉

1
Dance Party Freeze

How to play:

  • Play upbeat music and dance non-stop.
  • When the music stops, you MUST freeze in place! 🥶
  • Repeat for 5–7 minutes.
  • Add challenges like "jump in place," "spin around," or "move like a robot."

Benefits: Increases heart rate, stamina, and coordination.

Music idea: Party Freeze Dance Song — THE KIBOOMERS Preschool Songs for Circle Time

2
Running Obstacle Course

How to play:

  • Set up an obstacle course using cones, jump ropes, pillows, or other objects.
  • Include challenges such as:
    • Zigzag running around cones
    • Jumping over small hurdles (pillows or markers)
    • Crawling under a rope (or imaginary tunnel)
    • Skipping to the finish line
  • Time yourself and try again — see if you can BEAT your time! ⏱️

Benefits: Improves endurance, agility, and coordination.

3
Jump Rope Challenge

How to play:

  • Get a jump rope or pretend you're holding one.
  • Start with basic jumps for 30 seconds.
  • Challenge yourself with different variations:
    • Fast jumping (see how many jumps in 30 seconds)
    • One-foot jumping (alternate legs)
    • Side-to-side jumps
    • Double jumps (jumping higher each time)

Benefits: Builds endurance, coordination, and cardiovascular fitness.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video showing your cardio moves! The more you do, the more points you earn. 🌟

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which cardio activity made your heart pound the loudest?
  • Did you feel more energized after?

Week 12

Week 12 Flight Club: Balance & Flow 🦋

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Wings out, balance ON — let's see how steady you can be! Three challenges to test your inner flamingo. 🦩

1
Flamingo Balance

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with your feet together.
  • Gently lift one foot and bend your knee so your foot is behind you.
  • Hold your arms out to the side like wings for balance.
  • Try to stay still like a flamingo for 10 seconds.
  • Switch legs and repeat.
  • Optional: Try closing one eye or flapping your "wings" for a fun challenge!

Benefits: Builds focus and body control.

2
Butterfly Stretch

How to do it:

  • Sit on the floor with feet together and knees bent outward.
  • Hold your feet with your hands and gently push your knees toward the floor.
  • Keep your back straight and hold the stretch.
  • Optional: Pretend your legs are butterfly wings and gently flap them! 🦋

Benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

3
Arm Circles

How to do it:

  • Stand up straight with your arms stretched out to the sides, like a big "T."
  • Slowly make small forward circles with your arms for 10 seconds.
  • Then switch directions and make small backward circles for 10 seconds.
  • Want a challenge? Try making the circles bigger each time!
  • Optional: Pretend you're flying like a superhero or spinning like a windmill!

Benefits: Warms up shoulder and arm muscles.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video demonstrating all three! 🌟

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • How long could you hold the flamingo balance?
  • Did one side feel easier than the other?

Week 14

Week 14 Flight Club: Power Up! 🦸

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Time to feel STRONG. Three power moves to make your muscles cheer. Heroes, assemble! 💪

1
Split Squat

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with one foot in front and the other foot behind you — like you're about to take a big step.
  • Keep your front knee over your ankle and your back heel lifted off the ground.
  • Slowly bend both knees to lower your body straight down.
  • Stop when your back knee is close to the ground (but not touching!).
  • Stand back up.
  • Do 5 slow squats, then switch legs and repeat.

Benefits: Strengthens leg muscles, especially thighs and calves.

2
Superhero Hold (Superman)

How to do it:

  • Lie flat on your stomach on the floor or a soft mat.
  • Stretch your arms straight out in front of you and your legs straight behind you.
  • At the same time, lift your arms, chest, and legs slightly off the ground.
  • Try to hold this pose for 10 seconds — like you're flying through the sky! 🦸
  • Slowly lower back down and rest.
  • Try it again 2–3 more times!

Benefits: Strengthens back and core muscles.

3
Bench Dips

How to do it:

  • Find a sturdy chair, bench, or low table.
  • Sit on the edge with your hands next to your hips.
  • Walk your feet forward and slide your bottom off the edge, so your hands are holding you up.
  • Bend your elbows to lower your body a little — like you're going down slowly.
  • Push back up until your arms are straight again.
  • Try doing 5–10 dips, then take a break!

Benefits: Strengthens arms, shoulders, and chest.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video of your power moves! The more you do, the more points you earn! 💥

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which move made your muscles feel the strongest?
  • Could you feel exactly which body parts were working?

2
Forearm Plank

How to do it:

  • Get into a plank position with forearms on the ground and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.
  • Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Seated Forward Stretch

How to do it:

  • Sit on the floor with legs straight in front of you.
  • Reach forward toward your toes while keeping your legs straight.
  • Hold the stretch for 10 seconds, then sit up slowly.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings and lower back.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video! 🌟

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which stretch was your favorite?
  • Did you notice your body feel less tense after?

discussions.title: Week 1: Why We Move
discussions.html:
Discussion Time! 🎉 Talk about WHY moving matters. Pick at least ONE question to answer, and reply to at least one classmate's post.

  • 💪 Why is exercise good for your heart?
  • 🤝 What does teamwork look like when you play games in PE?
  • 😄 How can physical activity help you feel better every day?

Tip: Real examples from YOUR life are the best — share a story!

discussions.title: Week 3: Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
discussions.html:
Warm-Up Discussion 🔥

Now that you've learned about warm-ups and cool-downs, share with your classmates!

  • Why is warming up SO important before exercise?
  • What's YOUR favorite warm-up move and why?
  • How do you feel during a cool-down? Calm? Sweaty? Tired in a good way?

Reply to at least one classmate and add something new — a tip, an idea, or just a "I love that move too!"

discussions.title: Week 5: Muscular Strength
discussions.html:
Strength Talk 💪

Strong muscles make life easier. Pick a question to discuss with your class:

  • What's something heavy you can lift now that you COULDN'T lift a year ago?
  • Which strength exercise sounds the most fun to try? Why?
  • Why do you think we need strong muscles in everyday life (not just sports)?

discussions.title: Week 7: Cardiovascular Fitness
discussions.html:
Cardio Chat ❤️

  • What's YOUR favorite way to do cardio? (Running? Dancing? Biking? Tag?)
  • How can you tell when your cardio system is working? (Hint: heart, lungs, sweat!)
  • What's one new cardio activity you'd be brave enough to try this month?

Reply to a classmate's post — bonus points for cheering them on!

discussions.title: Week 9: Flexibility & Stretching
discussions.html:
Flexibility Discussion 🤸

  • What part of your body is the LEAST flexible? (Be honest — most people have a tight spot!)
  • What's the silliest stretch you've ever done?
  • How does stretching make you feel — physically and mentally?

discussions.title: Week 11: Nutrition
discussions.html:
Nutrition Talk 🍎

  • What's your FAVORITE healthy food? Why?
  • What's the silliest healthy food you've ever tried? Did you like it?
  • What food group do you eat the MOST of? The LEAST of?

Be respectful — everyone eats different things, and that's okay!

discussions.title: Week 13: Locomotor Skills
discussions.html:
Locomotor Discussion 🚀

  • Which locomotor skill is the EASIEST for you? Which is the HARDEST?
  • Have you ever invented a new way to move? Describe it!
  • Why do you think babies have to LEARN how to walk?

discussions.title: Week 15: Throwing & Catching
discussions.html:
Throw & Catch Talk 🎯

  • Are you a better thrower or catcher? Why do you think?
  • What's the most amazing catch you've ever made (or seen)?
  • Why is hand-eye coordination important — even outside of sports?
